tasks.title: Counter
tasks.statement: Python: Counter(words). Write count_words(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, usize)>: word frequencies (split_whitespace, lowercase), in descending order of frequency, ties broken alphabetically.
tasks.hint: entry().or_insert(0) and sorting the pairs.

tasks.title: d.get(k, default)
tasks.statement: Python: d.get(k, 0). Write lookup(m: &HashMap<String, i32>, k: &str) -> i32 — the value for the key, or 0.
tasks.hint: get(k).copied().unwrap_or(0)

tasks.title: Invert a dictionary
tasks.statement: Python: {v: k for k, v in d.items()}. Write invert(m: &HashMap<String, i32>) -> HashMap<i32, String> (values are unique).
tasks.hint: iter().map(|(k, v)| (*v, k.clone())).collect()

tasks.title: Group by length
tasks.statement: Python: defaultdict(list). Write group_by_len(words: &[&str]) -> BTreeMap<usize, Vec<String>>: words by length in characters (in original order within each group).
tasks.hint: entry(len).or_default().push(…)

tasks.title: Anagram groups
tasks.statement: Write group_anagrams(words: &[&str]) -> Vec<Vec<String>>: anagram words together; the groups are sorted by their first word, and the words within groups are in original order. The key is the sorted letters.
tasks.hint: A Vec<char> key works: Vec implements Hash.

tasks.title: Two numbers in one pass
tasks.statement: Write two_sum(v: &[i32], target: i32) -> Option<(usize, usize)>: indices (i, j), i < j, with v[i] + v[j] = target, in a single pass with a HashMap “value → index”. For the first pair found as j advances.
tasks.hint: For each x, look for target - x among those already seen.

tasks.title: Merge with addition
tasks.statement: Python: Counter(a) + Counter(b). Write merge_sum(a: &HashMap<String, i32>, b: &HashMap<String, i32>) -> BTreeMap<String, i32>: the keys are combined, and values are added when keys coincide.
tasks.hint: Walk both maps and accumulate into one.

tasks.title: dict(zip(k, v))
tasks.statement: Write zip_map(keys: &[&str], vals: &[i32]) -> BTreeMap<String, i32> — pairs up to the shorter of the two slices.
tasks.hint: zip + collect into BTreeMap.

tasks.title: Top words
tasks.statement: Write top_words(text: &str, n: usize) -> Vec<String>: the n most frequent words (lowercase); ties in frequency are broken alphabetically.
tasks.hint: Count first, then sort_by and take(n).

tasks.title: and_modify
tasks.statement: Write apply(events: &[(&str, i32)]) -> BTreeMap<String, i32>: for each event (key, value) — if the key already exists, add the value, otherwise set it (and_modify + or_insert).
tasks.hint: m.entry(k).and_modify(|e| *e += v).or_insert(v)

tasks.title: Key range
tasks.statement: Write between(m: &BTreeMap<i32, String>, lo: i32, hi: i32) -> Vec<String>: the values for keys in [lo, hi] in ascending key order (the range method).
tasks.hint: m.range(lo..=hi)

tasks.title: Minimum and maximum key
tasks.statement: Write extremes(m: &BTreeMap<i32, i32>) -> Option<(i32, i32)>: (smallest key, largest key) or None for an empty map (first_key_value, last_key_value).
tasks.hint: first_key_value() returns Option<(&K, &V)>.

tasks.title: Set operations
tasks.statement: Write set_ops(a: &[i32], b: &[i32]) -> (Vec<i32>, Vec<i32>, Vec<i32>): the union, the intersection, and the difference a − b, each result sorted in ascending order.
tasks.hint: union, intersection, difference are iterators; collect into a Vec and sort.

tasks.title: How many distinct
tasks.statement: Python: len(set(l)). Write distinct(v: &[i32]) -> usize.
tasks.hint: collect into a HashSet and len().

tasks.title: Any duplicates
tasks.statement: Write has_duplicates(v: &[i32]) -> bool in linear time: a HashSet and an early exit on a repeat (insert returns false).
tasks.hint: if !seen.insert(x) { return true; }

tasks.title: Common letters
tasks.statement: Write common(a: &str, b: &str) -> String: the letters present in both strings (without repeats), in alphabetical order.
tasks.hint: The intersection of two HashSet<char>.

tasks.title: Pangram
tasks.statement: Write is_pangram(s: &str) -> bool: whether the string contains all 26 Latin letters (case doesn't matter).
tasks.hint: Collect a set of letters and check its size.

tasks.title: First non-repeating
tasks.statement: Python: Counter + a pass. Write first_unique(v: &[i32]) -> Option<i32>: the first element that occurs exactly once.
tasks.hint: The first pass counts, the second looks for count == 1.

tasks.title: Character histogram
tasks.statement: Write histogram(s: &str) -> BTreeMap<char, usize>: how many times each character occurs (excluding spaces).
tasks.hint: BTreeMap keeps keys sorted.

tasks.title: Warehouse
tasks.statement: Write update_stock(stock: &mut HashMap<String, u32>, op: &str, item: &str, n: u32) -> Result<(), String>: «add» increases the stock; «take» decreases it (Err("нет товара") if the key is missing, and Err("мало") if the stock is less than n; when the stock reaches 0 the key is removed); any other operation — Err("операция").
tasks.hint: get_mut gives &mut to the value; remove at zero.

tasks.title: Word index
tasks.statement: Write build_index(docs: &[&str]) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<usize>>: for each word (lowercase) — the numbers of the documents (from 0, without repeats, ascending) where it occurs.
tasks.hint: Check last() before push so you don't duplicate a number.

tasks.title: Memoization
tasks.statement: Write fib(n: u64, memo: &mut HashMap<u64, u64>) -> u64 with memoization (like @lru_cache): fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1. For n = 90 the computation is instant.
tasks.hint: Look in memo first, then compute and store.

tasks.title: Lookup table
tasks.statement: Write roman_to_int(s: &str) -> u32: a Roman numeral to an ordinary number (I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000; a smaller digit before a larger one is subtracted). Use a HashMap<char, u32> or match.
tasks.hint: If the next digit is larger, subtract the current one.

tasks.title: Cache with a limit
tasks.statement: Implement a struct Cache with the fields map: HashMap<String, i32>, order: Vec<String>, cap: usize. The function new(cap) creates an empty cache; put(&mut self, k: &str, v: i32) adds a pair and, when cap is exceeded, evicts the oldest key (FIFO); updating an existing key doesn't change the order; get(&self, k: &str) -> Option<i32>.
tasks.hint: On eviction, remove the first element of order and its key from map.

tasks.title: Bidirectional mapping
tasks.statement: Write is_isomorphic(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool: can the letters of a be replaced by letters of b to get b (each letter maps to the same one, different letters to different ones; the strings have equal length).
tasks.hint: Two maps: a → b and b → a.

tasks.title: Vertex degrees of a graph
tasks.statement: Write degrees(edges: &[(u32, u32)]) -> BTreeMap<u32, usize>: the degree of each vertex of an undirected graph (each edge increases the degree of both endpoints; a loop (v, v) counts twice).
tasks.hint: Two entry calls per edge.

tasks.title: Adjacency list
tasks.statement: Write adjacency(edges: &[(u32, u32)]) -> BTreeMap<u32, Vec<u32>>: for each vertex — a sorted list of the neighbors in an undirected graph, without repeats.
tasks.hint: or_default().push in both directions; then sort and dedup.

tasks.title: Sort by value
tasks.statement: Python: sorted(d.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]). Write by_value(m: &HashMap<String, i32>) -> Vec<(String, i32)>: pairs in ascending order of value, ties broken by key.
tasks.hint: sort_by with then to break ties.

tasks.title: Struct as a key
tasks.statement: Add the needed derives (Hash, PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Copy, Debug) to the struct Pos { x: i32, y: i32 } and write visited(path: &[(i32, i32)]) -> usize: how many distinct cells were visited (HashSet<Pos>).
tasks.hint: #[derive(Hash, PartialEq, Eq)] makes a struct usable as a key.

tasks.title: What changed
tasks.statement: Write changed(old: &[&str], new: &[&str]) -> Vec<String>: the words that are in exactly one of the lists (the symmetric difference), in alphabetical order.
tasks.hint: symmetric_difference returns an iterator.
